---
title: "05 – Does S. aureus phosphorylate histidine?"
subtitle: "Bio253 HS2026 · STY vs STYH search, judged conservatively"
---

**Claim to test:** Prust *et al.* 2021 (*Mol Cell Proteomics* 20:100034) report that
~8 % of all *S. aureus* phospho-sites are on **histidine** (pHis). Can we see pHis
in our data – and how sure can we be?

The raw files were searched twice:

* **STY** – phosphorylation allowed on Ser, Thr, Tyr
* **STYH** – additionally on His

::: {.callout-important}
## Be sceptical – on purpose
* pHis is **acid-labile**. Our workflow (Fe-IMAC enrichment, acidic LC) is not
  pHis-friendly, so many pHis may be lost – and the ones we "see" need extra scrutiny.
* The main source of false pHis is **mis-localisation**: if a peptide also contains
  S, T or Y, the search engine may put the phosphate on H although it sits on a
  neighbour – or the other way round.
* Allowing H as an extra acceptor makes the search space bigger, which by itself
  creates some extra (false) hits.

We therefore treat pHis **very conservatively**. You will build evidence tiers yourself.
:::

```{r setup}
source("../R/setup.R")
# keep contaminants here: we want the complete peptide lists of both searches
styh <- read_sites("STYH", drop_contaminants = FALSE)
sty  <- read_sites("STY",  drop_contaminants = FALSE)
```

## 1. How many sites per residue in the two searches?

```{r residues}
bind_rows(styh, sty) |>
  distinct(search, site_id, residue) |>
  count(search, residue) |>
  pivot_wider(names_from = search, values_from = n, values_fill = 0)
```

**Question:** the STYH search finds more sites in total. Are the additional sites
only His sites, or do S/T/Y counts also change? Why might they?

## 2. Localisation probability

`best_loc_prob` = best localisation probability of a site over all samples
(1 = the search engine is sure the phosphate sits on exactly this residue).

```{r lp-distribution, fig.height=4}
site_level <- distinct(styh, site_id, residue, best_loc_prob)

ggplot(site_level, aes(best_loc_prob, colour = residue)) +
  stat_ecdf(linewidth = 0.8) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 0.75, linetype = "dashed") +
  labs(x = "best localisation probability", y = "fraction of sites with LP <= x",
       title = "STYH search: localisation probability per residue")

site_level |>
  mutate(lp_class = lp_class(best_loc_prob)) |>
  count(residue, lp_class) |>
  pivot_wider(names_from = lp_class, values_from = n, values_fill = 0)
```

**Question:** Are His sites localised as well as S/T/Y sites? How many His sites
have LP ≥ 0.75?

## 3. One evidence table for every His site

We now collect, for every His site, the evidence we need. Read each step.

### 3a. Sites, localisation and reproducibility

**Reproducibility is judged from the intensity** (detected = intensity > 0), not from
the per-sample localisation probabilities: FragPipe sometimes reports an LP for a
sample in which the site was *not quantified*.

```{r lp-filled}
styh |>
  filter(residue == "H") |>
  summarise(sample_rows = n(),
            quantified = sum(!is.na(intensity)),
            LP_reported_but_not_quantified = sum(is.na(intensity) & loc_prob_fragpipe > 0,
                                                 na.rm = TRUE))
```

```{r evidence-1}
his <- styh |>
  filter(residue == "H") |>
  group_by(site_id, locus_tag, product, peptide, best_loc_prob) |>
  summarise(
    n_samples_quant = sum(!is.na(intensity)),                  # of 27
    n_samples_lp075 = sum(loc_prob_fragpipe >= 0.75, na.rm = TRUE),  # FragPipe LPs, for reference only
    max_reps_in_group = max(tapply(!is.na(intensity), group, sum)),  # best group, of 3
    .groups = "drop") |>
  mutate(lp_class = lp_class(best_loc_prob))
nrow(his)
```

### 3b. Is there an alternative acceptor on the peptide?

If the peptide contains **no S, T or Y at all**, the phosphate cannot be
mis-placed onto a neighbouring S/T/Y. That is the strongest kind of evidence we can
get from the search alone. A `Peptide` entry can contain several sequence variants
separated by `;` – we take the variant with the fewest S/T/Y.

```{r evidence-2}
peptide_variants("ANhEQIIEAIK;MANhEQIIEAIK")   # example: two variants, upper-cased
n_sty_acceptors("ANhEQIIEAIK;MANhEQIIEAIK")

his <- his |>
  mutate(n_sty_acceptors = n_sty_acceptors(peptide),
         no_alt_acceptor = n_sty_acceptors == 0,
         co_phospho_STY  = co_phospho_sty(peptide))
count(his, no_alt_acceptor)
```

### 3c. Does the STY-only search explain the same peptide?

If the very same peptide was also identified as a phosphopeptide in the STY search,
the spectrum can be explained **without** pHis. FragPipe writes phospho residues in
lower case, so we compare upper-cased sequences. We count a His peptide as
"explained" only if **all** its variants appear in the STY search.

```{r evidence-3}
sty_peptides <- phosphopeptide_set(sty)
his <- his |>
  mutate(seen_in_STY_search   = all_variants_in(peptide, sty_peptides),
         partly_in_STY_search = any_variant_in(peptide, sty_peptides))
count(his, no_alt_acceptor, seen_in_STY_search)
```

## 4. Worked example: HPr His15

HPr (phosphocarrier protein of the PTS sugar uptake system) carries a **textbook
pHis at His15** – the phosphate is transferred from enzyme I to HPr-His15 and on to
sugar transporters. If we find any real pHis, HPr should be a candidate.

```{r hpr-find}
hpr <- find_protein("B7H15_05615") |> select(locus_tag, product, protein_key, staa8_uniprot)
hpr
```

The same HPr peptide in the two searches:

```{r hpr-compare}
hpr_peptide <- "MEQNSYVIIDETGIHAR"
bind_rows(styh, sty) |>
  filter(protein_key %in% hpr$protein_key,
         str_detect(toupper(peptide), hpr_peptide)) |>
  group_by(search, site_id, residue, position, peptide, best_loc_prob) |>
  summarise(n_samples_quant = sum(!is.na(intensity)), .groups = "drop") |>
  arrange(search, position)
```

**Questions**

* In the STY search, where is the phosphate placed on this peptide? In STYH?
* Which interpretation is chemically / biologically more plausible, and why?
* Is the STY-search interpretation "wrong" – or simply the best it could do without H?
* Does this single example prove that pHis survives our workflow?

## 5. His sites on proteins that *should* carry pHis

Classical pHis proteins in bacteria: **histidine kinases** of two-component systems
(autophosphorylation on His, transfer to Asp of the response regulator – note:
pAsp was not searched), **HPr** and **enzyme I** of the PTS, and some metabolic
enzymes (e.g. succinyl-CoA synthetase, nucleoside-diphosphate kinase).

```{r canonical}
canonical_pattern <- "histidine kinase|phosphocarrier|PTS|phosphoenolpyruvate|response regulator|succinate--CoA|nucleoside-diphosphate kinase"
find_protein(canonical_pattern) |> count(product, sort = TRUE)

his |>
  filter(str_detect(product, regex(canonical_pattern, ignore_case = TRUE))) |>
  select(locus_tag, product, site_id, peptide, best_loc_prob, n_sty_acceptors,
         seen_in_STY_search, max_reps_in_group)
```

**Question:** Do any histidine kinases show a His site? Is the site at the
conserved, autophosphorylated His (look at the protein in UniProt via
`staa8_uniprot`)? What about the many His sites on proteins that are *not* known
pHis proteins?

## 6. Your task: build confidence tiers

Combine the evidence into **tiers**, from "strongest candidate" to "unreliable".
Suggested criteria (you decide the order and thresholds – and justify them!):

| evidence | column |
|---|---|
| no alternative S/T/Y acceptor on the peptide | `no_alt_acceptor` |
| well localised | `best_loc_prob >= 0.75` |
| reproducible: ≥ 2 of 3 replicates in some group | `max_reps_in_group >= 2` |
| peptide **not** explained by the STY search | `!seen_in_STY_search` |

Write your tiers below (set `eval: true` once you filled in the conditions).
Number tiers 1 (strongest) to 6 (weakest) and **start every label with the number**.

```{r my-tiers}
#| eval: false
my_tiers <- his |>
  mutate(tier = case_when(
    no_alt_acceptor & ______ & ______  ~ "1 strongest: ...",
    no_alt_acceptor & ______           ~ "2 ...",
    no_alt_acceptor                    ~ "3 ...",
    ______ & !seen_in_STY_search       ~ "4 ...",
    ______                             ~ "5 ...",
    TRUE                               ~ "6 unreliable"))
count(my_tiers, tier)
```

Check your tiers against the lecturer's reference (counts only – it tells you
*how many* sites agree, not *which*):

```{r check}
#| eval: false
check_his_tiers(my_tiers)
```

## 7. Real or artefact? A decision framework

For each candidate, go through this list and write your verdict in your lab notebook.

1. **Chemistry:** acid-labile pHis + acidic workflow → is it plausible the site survived?
2. **Localisation:** LP ≥ 0.75? Any S/T/Y on the peptide? Same peptide explained by STY?
3. **Reproducibility:** seen in ≥ 2/3 replicates of a group? In more than one group?
4. **Biology:** is the protein a known His-phosphorylated protein? Is the His conserved?
5. **Spectra:** (beyond this course, but name it) inspect the MS2 spectra – are there
   fragment ions that pin the phosphate to H? pHis shows characteristic neutral
   losses (e.g. −80, −98, −116 Da).
6. **Orthogonal validation:** pHis-specific antibodies, non-acidic enrichment, mutation
   of the His.

**Discussion:** after this analysis, how would you phrase our evidence for (or against)
the claim of Prust *et al.*? Distinguish "we found no evidence" from "we found evidence
of absence".

sessionInfo()
